skill.name: Claude Skills Meta-Skill
skill.description: A meta-skill that turns scattered domain material such as docs, APIs, code, and specs into a reusable Claude Skill. It produces a SKILL.md entrypoint plus references, scripts, and assets, and refactors existing skills for clarity, reliable activation, and quality gates.
skill.summary: Build and refactor reusable Claude Skills with reliable activation and a built-in quality gate.
skill.author: 2025Emma

security_audit.summary: This is a benign meta-skill for authoring and validating Claude Skills, containing only Markdown documentation and two pure Bash helper scripts that use standard POSIX tooling with no network access. All 30 static findings were adjudicated as false positives: the 'external_commands' hits are Markdown backticks in prose and ordinary shell variable assignments (basename, dirname, awk, mktemp) operating on script-relative or user-supplied skill paths; the 'filesystem' hits are literal '../' relative links in docs and script-relative asset resolution; the 'blocker/system-reconnaissance' and 'metadata' hits are documentation text and a frontmatter-parse note. No data exfiltration, credential access, prompt injection, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md frontmatter could not be statically parsed (flagged as invalid_frontmatter), likely due to a leading 'TRANSLATED CONTENT:' line before the '---' YAML delimiter.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the leading 'TRANSLATED CONTENT:' marker so the first line of SKILL.md is the '---' frontmatter delimiter, which lets automated scanners and the skill's own validate-skill.sh parse the name and description fields.

Standard idiom to resolve the script's own directory: script_dir="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)". Operates only on the script's own path, no user-controlled or network input. Safe and conventional.
assets_dir="${script_dir}/../assets" resolves the bundled assets directory relative to the script's own location. It reads the skill's own template files; it is not attacker-controlled traversal.

base_name="$(basename -- "${skill_dir%/}")" extracts the directory basename from the user-supplied skill directory argument. Uses '--' to prevent option injection; no shell metacharacter execution. Safe.
Command substitution capturing awk output that parses SKILL.md YAML frontmatter. Reads a local file with a fixed awk program; no dynamic command construction. Safe.
Command substitution running a fixed awk script over the parsed frontmatter to extract the 'name' field. Static, local text processing only. Safe.
Command substitution running a fixed awk script to extract the 'description' field from frontmatter. Local text parsing, no dynamic execution. Safe.
filtered_md="$(mktemp)" creates a temporary file via the standard mktemp utility, paired with a trap that removes it on EXIT. Conventional, safe temp-file handling.
Command substitution running awk to find the line number of the 'Quick Reference' heading in a local filtered Markdown file. Fixed program, local input. Safe.
awk command substitution locating the end of the Quick Reference section by line number in a local file. Static text processing. Safe.
total_lines="$(wc -l < "$filtered_md" | tr -d ' ')" counts lines in a local temp file. Standard, read-only shell utilities. Safe.
quick_end="$((total_lines + 1))" is pure arithmetic expansion, not command substitution. No external command; entirely deterministic integer math. Safe.
quick_len="$((quick_end - quick_start - 1))" is arithmetic expansion computing a section length. No command execution. Safe.
awk command substitution locating the 'Examples' heading line number in a local file. Fixed program, local read-only input. Safe.
awk command substitution finding the end of the Examples section by line number in a local file. Static text parsing. Safe.

Command substitution running a fixed awk program that counts '### Example' headings within the Examples section of a local file. Static, local text analysis. Safe.
mktemp creates a temporary work file for stripping fenced code blocks before section checks. The file is cleaned up via a trap on EXIT. Standard, safe temp-file usage.
This is an error-message string in a validation guard: die "Invalid name: '$name' (expected ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$)". It rejects malformed skill names; it performs no system reconnaissance.

Manual review of SKILL.md confirms it is a benign meta-skill document. The frontmatter parse failed only because a leading 'TRANSLATED CONTENT:' line precedes the '---' delimiter; the actual name/description frontmatter and body content are legitimate and non-malicious. Flagged for author cleanup, not a security risk.

content.user_title: Build Reliable Claude Skills From Any Source
content.value_statement: Scattered docs, APIs, and specs are hard to turn into a skill that activates reliably and stays maintainable. This meta-skill guides you to produce a clean SKILL.md, structured references, and a validated quality gate every time.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of a new Claude Skill from docs, specs, or repositories, producing a structured SKILL.md with frontmatter, triggers, and boundaries.
Refactors an existing skill that is too long or unclear by splitting long content into a references directory with a navigable index.
Provides a create-skill.sh script that scaffolds minimal or full skill directory layouts from bundled templates.
Provides a validate-skill.sh script that checks YAML frontmatter, required section headings, Quick Reference size, and example count, with an optional strict mode.
Supplies a documented quality gate checklist and scoring rubric to review a skill before delivery.
Includes reference guides on skill specifications and common anti-patterns to improve activation reliability.
limitations: The validator is heuristic and assumes the recommended section headings; it does not deeply parse arbitrary Markdown structures.
It builds skills but is not a domain skill itself, so it does not supply domain knowledge for any specific technology.
The scripts require a Bash shell with standard POSIX tools such as awk, sed, grep, and mktemp.
It does not verify external facts, so any unproven claims must be checked separately by the author.

use_cases.title: Turn official documentation into a skill
use_cases.description: A developer takes a product's official docs and code samples and produces a reusable skill with decidable triggers and reproducible examples.
use_cases.target_user: Software developer creating internal tooling skills

use_cases.title: Refactor an overgrown skill
use_cases.description: A maintainer splits a bloated SKILL.md into a short Quick Reference plus organized reference files, improving clarity and activation reliability.
use_cases.target_user: Skill maintainer cleaning up legacy skills

use_cases.title: Enforce a quality gate before publishing
use_cases.description: A team lead runs the validator and checklist across candidate skills to enforce consistent structure and quality before release.
use_cases.target_user: Team lead standardizing a skill library

prompt_templates.title: Create a skill from a document
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Claude Skills meta-skill to turn this documentation into a new skill. Extract the key patterns, define clear activation triggers, and produce a SKILL.md with at least three reproducible examples.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner starting a new skill from source material

prompt_templates.title: Scaffold a skill directory
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the meta-skill to scaffold a full skill layout named data-pipeline. Generate the SKILL.md, references index, and placeholder reference files, then explain what to fill in next.
prompt_templates.scenario: Setting up the initial structure for a new skill

prompt_templates.title: Refactor and split a long skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this existing SKILL.md. Keep only short, directly usable patterns in the Quick Reference and move long-form explanations into a references directory with a navigable index.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate cleanup of a bloated skill

prompt_templates.title: Run the full quality gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate this skill against the quality gate. Check the frontmatter, required sections, Quick Reference length, and example count, then apply the scoring rubric and list every fix needed before publishing.

output_examples.input: Turn this API documentation into a new skill called payments-api.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a payments-api directory with a SKILL.md entrypoint, a references index, and placeholder reference files. The SKILL.md includes frontmatter with a decidable description, a When to Use section, a Not For section, a short Quick Reference of key patterns, and three end-to-end examples.

output_examples.input: Validate the skill in skills/payments-api using strict mode.
output_examples.output: The validator reports whether the frontmatter name and description are present and well formed, whether all required section headings exist, whether the Quick Reference is within the recommended length, and whether at least three examples are present. In strict mode it stops on the first failing check and prints the exact issue to fix.

best_practices: Write the frontmatter description as what plus when, using concrete trigger keywords so activation is decidable.
Keep the Quick Reference short and directly usable, and move any long-form explanation into the references directory.
Run the validator in strict mode and the quality checklist before considering a skill ready to publish.
anti_patterns: Pasting large blocks of raw documentation into SKILL.md instead of extracting concise, reusable patterns.
Writing a vague description such as helps with X, which makes the skill activate unpredictably.
Skipping the Not For and Boundaries section, which leads to the skill misfiring on unrelated requests.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a structured Claude Skill: a SKILL.md entrypoint plus optional references, scripts, and assets, organized for reliable activation and easy maintenance.

faq.question: Do I need to run the shell scripts?
faq.answer: No. The create-skill.sh and validate-skill.sh scripts are optional helpers. You can author and review a skill by hand using the templates and checklist instead.

faq.question: What do the helper scripts require?
faq.answer: They require a Bash shell and common POSIX tools such as awk, sed, grep, and mktemp. They do not require any network access.

faq.question: Does this skill provide domain knowledge?
faq.answer: No. It is a meta-skill for building other skills. Domain knowledge belongs in the specific skills you create with it.

faq.question: How does strict validation differ from basic validation?
faq.answer: Basic validation prints warnings for missing sections and heuristics. Strict validation enforces the recommended section layout and stops on the first failing check.

faq.question: Is this skill safe to install?
faq.answer: Yes. The audit found only Markdown documentation and two local Bash helper scripts that use standard tools with no network access, and no malicious behavior was detected.
